sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: AN EXTENSIVE/SLIGHTLY POSITIVE TILT LONGWAVE TROUGH...ACCOMPANIED BY A STRONG DEEP LAYER WIND FIELD...WILL GENERALLY SHIFT EASTWARD/FRAGMENT THROUGH THE PERIOD...WITH ONE PORTION CROSSING ONTARIO/QUEBEC AND THE ADJACENT GREAT LAKES REGION...WITH THE SOUTHERN SPLIT/BASAL PORTION OVERSPREADING THE MID-SOUTH/TN VALLEY AND GULF COAST STATES. THE PRIMARY COLD FRONT...AUGMENTED BY EARLY DAY CONVECTION/EXISTING COLD POOLS...WILL SPREAD EASTWARD ACROSS THE GREAT LAKES REGION AND OH/TN VALLEYS AND LOWER MS VALLEY TODAY...AND EVENTUALLY SHIFT TO NEAR/EAST OF THE APPALACHIANS LATE TONIGHT.

sections.title: UPPER OH VALLEY/NORTHEAST STATES/MID-ATLANTIC STATES
sections.text: AS PREVIOUSLY MENTIONED...THE NORTHERN SPLIT OF A LONGWAVE TROUGH WILL CROSS ONTARIO/QUEBEC AND THE ADJACENT GREAT LAKES REGION TODAY. BANDS OF SHOWERS/TSTMS ARE LIKELY TO BE ONGOING EARLY TODAY ALONG/AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT ACROSS SOUTHERN PORTIONS OF ONTARIO/QUEBEC AND THE LOWER GREAT LAKES REGION TO THE OH VALLEY. A VEERING WEST-SOUTHWESTERLY 40-55 KT LOW LEVEL JET WILL CONTINUE TO TRANSPORT A RELATIVELY MOIST AIRMASS TOWARD THE NORTHEAST STATES FROM THE MIDWEST. WITH TIME...AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT AND ONGOING EARLY DAY CONVECTION...CONTINUED MOISTENING/GRADUAL DESTABILIZATION SHOULD SUPPORT A RENEWED UPSWING IN CONVECTIVE COVERAGE/VIGOR BY AFTERNOON. IT APPEARS THE GREATEST DESTABILIZATION SHOULD OCCUR FROM PORTIONS OF KY AND SOUTHERN OH/MUCH OF WV INTO PA/NY AND PERHAPS EVEN WESTERN NEW ENGLAND DURING THE AFTERNOON...WHERE UPWARDS OF 1000-1500 J/KG OF MLCAPE WILL BE POSSIBLE. VERY STRONG/LARGELY-UNIDIRECTIONAL SOUTHWESTERLY LOW/MID TROPOSPHERIC WINDS WILL BE QUITE SUPPORTIVE OF AN ORGANIZED/QUASI-LINEAR DAMAGING WIND EVENT AS STORMS ORGANIZE INTO LINES/LINE SEGMENTS ALONG AND EAST OF THE COLD FRONT THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. sections.title: TN VALLEY/GULF COAST STATES
sections.text: THE PREVIOUSLY DISCUSSED SOUTHERN/BASAL SHORTWAVE TROUGH IS EXPECTED TO SHIFT EASTWARD OVER THE ARKLATEX/MID-SOUTH TO THE TN VALLEY/GULF COAST STATES THROUGH TONIGHT. ALONG/JUST AHEAD OF A THE EAST-SOUTHEAST ADVANCING COLD FRONT...BROKEN BANDS OF RELATIVELY WELL-ORGANIZED QUASI-LINEAR STORMS WILL BE ONGOING THIS MORNING IN A SPATIALLY EXTENSIVE NORTHEAST-SOUTHWEST ORIENTED CORRIDOR FROM NEAR THE CONFLUENCE OF THE OH/MS RIVERS TO THE MID-SOUTH/ARKLATEX REGIONS. SOME OF THESE COULD BE STRONG/SEVERE AT LEAST IN AN ISOLATED SENSE...WITH THE PRIMARY SEVERE RISK OF DAMAGING WINDS. A SOMEWHAT NARROW /GULF COAST VICINITY ASIDE/ MOIST INFLUX WILL OCCUR TODAY TOWARD THE TN VALLEY...AHEAD OF A WHAT SHOULD BE A REJUVENATION OF DEEP CONVECTION DURING THE DAY ALONG THE COLD FRONT...OR PERHAPS MORE LIKELY FOCUSED ALONG AND EAST-SOUTHEAST OF EARLY DAY OUTFLOW-INDUCED EFFECTIVE BOUNDARIES. IT WOULD SEEM THE RELATIVELY STRONGEST DESTABILIZATION /1000-2000 J PER KG MLCAPE/ AND RESULTANT CONVECTIVE UPSWING THIS AFTERNOON SHOULD OCCUR FROM EASTERN LA INTO MS/AL AND PERHAPS EVENTUALLY MIDDLE/EASTERN TN AND WESTERN GA. sections.title: PORTIONS OF TN/OH AND LOWER MS VALLEY
sections.text: ALL MODELS ARE IN GENERAL AGREEMENT THAT ONGOING CONVECTIVE LINE WILL ONLY SLOWLY INTENSIFY THIS MORNING DUE TO WARM MID LEVEL TEMPERATURES SHOWN ON 12Z BMX/JAN/BNA RAOBS. HOWEVER...APPROACH OF UPPER TROUGH AND DAYTIME HEATING WILL ERODE CAP AND LEAD TO SEVERE STORMS BY EARLY AFTERNOON. LOW LEVEL CYCLOGENESIS IS EXPECTED OVER KY/TN BY MID AFTERNOON...WITH INCREASING LOW LEVEL VERTICAL SHEAR OVER THE WARM SECTOR. FORECAST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST 0-3KM SRH VALUES EXCEEDING 300 M2/S2...BUT ALSO SHOW A CONTINUED MID LEVEL INVERSION WHICH MAY LIMIT UPDRAFT STRENGTH. FOR THIS REASON...HAVE NOT UPGRADED TO MODERATE RISK AT THIS TIME. HOWEVER...AN UPGRADE MAY OCCUR LATER TODAY IF CONCERNS REGARDING THERMODYNAMICS ARE LESSENED. REGARDLESS...POTENTIAL FOR A FEW TORNADOES AND CONSIDERABLE WIND DAMAGE REMAINS FROM NORTHEAST MS INTO MUCH OF MIDDLE TN/AL AND SOUTHERN KY. STORMS MAY AFFECT PORTIONS OF NORTH GA TONIGHT BEFORE DIMINISHING. ...NY/PA INTO CENTRAL APPALACHIANS. MODEL GUIDANCE IS IN AGREEMENT THAT A RATHER POTENT ENVIRONMENT WILL DEVELOP LATER TODAY AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT FROM SOUTHERN NY AND MUCH OF PA INTO WV/VA. sections.title: WIDESPREAD DAMAGING WIND EVENT POSSIBLE TODAY INTO TONIGHT
sections.text: ...KY/TN INTO LOWER MS VALLEY AND CNTRL GULF COAST STATES... A FOCUSED CORRIDOR OF DCVA ASSOCIATED WITH VIGOROUS VORTICITY MAXIMUM OVER THE SRN PLAINS COMBINED WITH A COUPLED UPPER-LEVEL JET STRUCTURE WILL ENHANCE DEEP ASCENT ACROSS THE REGION TODAY. DEEPENING SURFACE LOW ATTENDANT TO THE SRN PLAINS VORTICITY MAXIMUM /ANALYZED OVER CNTRL AR AS OF 15Z/ WILL DEVELOP NEWD TO VICINITY OF S-CNTRL KY OR NRN-MIDDLE TN BY LATE AFTERNOON...REACHING THE VA PIEDMONT BY 12/12Z. TRAILING COLD FRONT WILL ADVANCE EWD/SEWD THROUGH THE LOWER MS VALLEY AND CNTRL GULF COAST STATES. 12Z REGIONAL SOUNDINGS ACROSS WARM SECTOR SHOWED THE PRESENCE OF RATHER WARM MIDLEVEL TEMPERATURES ALONG ANTICYCLONIC SIDE OF MIDLEVEL JET CORE WHICH WERE RESULTING IN POOR LAPSE RATES. HOWEVER...VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY DOES SUGGEST THAT RELATIVELY STRONG DIABATIC HEATING WILL OCCUR TODAY ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR. WHEN COUPLED WITH COOLING MIDLEVEL TEMPERATURES /IN ASSOCIATION WITH 12-HR HEIGHT FALLS OF 100-150 M AT 500 MB/...AIR MASS IS EXPECTED TO BECOME WEAKLY TO MODERATELY UNSTABLE WITH MLCAPE VALUES RANGING FROM 500-1000 J/KG OVER THE TN VALLEY TO 1000-1500 J/KG ALONG THE GULF COAST. sections.title: MID-ATLANTIC/NORTHEAST STATES
sections.text: TSTMS HAVE GENERALLY STRUGGLED TO DEVELOP MUCH OF THE DAY...PROBABLY ATTRIBUTABLE TO FACTORS SUCH AS CLOUD COVER AND LIMITED FORCING ON THE LARGE SCALE/MODEST MASS CONVERGENCE IN THE WAKE OF THE QUEBEC UPPER TROUGH. HOWEVER...ISOLATED TO SCATTERED TSTMS HAVE DEVELOPED LATE THIS AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING FROM NORTHERN MD INTO WESTERN NEW ENGLAND AMID A ZONE OF DIFFERENTIAL HEATING/PRE-COLD FRONTAL CONFLUENCE. ANY SUSTAINED/MATURE UPDRAFTS COULD POSE A SHORT TERM SEVERE THREAT YET THIS EVENING GIVEN A HIGH DEGREE OF VERTICAL SHEAR...BUT AN ORGANIZED/SUSTAINED SEVERE RISK IS NOT ANTICIPATED. ..GUYER.. 04/12/2011
